mainTopic: A thief who slaughters a stolen קדשים animal: can the שחיטה count as the act that 'permits' the animal, when really זריקה or פדיה is what permits it?
overview: The גמרא is explaining how a thief can owe the fourfold or fivefold payment for slaughtering a stolen consecrated animal. After explanations given in the name of רבי יוחנן (slaughter inside the מקדש), ריש לקיש gives his own case: slaughtering blemished consecrated animals outside. רבי אלעזר objects to both. Inside, it is the זריקה of the blood that permits the meat. For a blemished animal, it is the פדיה that permits it. So the slaughter alone does not seem to permit anything. The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר forgot רבי שמעון's rule: what is ready to be sprinkled counts as sprinkled, and what is ready to be redeemed counts as redeemed. It proves the sprinkling half from a ברייתא about נותר. Meat left overnight after the blood was fit to be sprinkled can get טומאת אוכלין, even though the blood was never actually sprinkled. The amud ends as the גמרא begins a second ברייתא of רבי שמעון to prove the redemption half, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the case is slaughtering blemished animals outside
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that the case is a thief who slaughters blemished consecrated animals outside the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש said: it is talking about someone who slaughters blemished animals outside.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives his own way of picturing the case, different from the explanations given in the name of רבי יוחנן. In his case, the thief slaughters a consecrated animal that has a מום, outside the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A consecrated animal with a מום cannot be brought as a קרבן. It may be slaughtered outside the מקדש and eaten once it is redeemed. So ריש לקיש moves the case away from the מקדש altogether.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, the study partner of רבי יוחנן
Animals with a blemish that makes them unfit for the מזבח
Outside the מקדש
Slaughters

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
It is a case where he slaughters blemished animals outside.
phrases.notes: These are consecrated animals with a blemish. They can't go on the מזבח, so they're slaughtered outside the מקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different case from the earlier explanations given in the name of רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The thief's liability is pictured as slaughtering blemished consecrated animals outside the מקדש.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's challenge to רבי יוחנן: sprinkling is what permits
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks how the slaughter in רבי יוחנן's case counts, when it is the זריקה of the blood that permits the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר wondered about this: According to רבי יוחנן, does the slaughter make it permitted? Doesn't the sprinkling make it permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר raises a difficulty with רבי יוחנן's explanations, which deal with a קרבן slaughtered inside the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a קרבן, the meat is not permitted right after the שחיטה. It becomes permitted only after the blood is sprinkled on the מזבח. So the thief's slaughter does not seem to be the act that makes the animal permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: He wondered about it (raised a difficulty)
An אמורא, a student of רבי יוחנן
The slaughter permits (the meat)
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar wondered about this:
According to Rabbi Yochanan, does the slaughter permit it?!
phrases.notes: He means the explanations given in the name of רבי יוחנן, where the animal is slaughtered inside the מקדש.

phrases.english: But isn't it the sprinkling that permits it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanations of רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's case of a קרבן slaughtered inside the מקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For a קרבן, the זריקה permits the meat, not the שחיטה, so the slaughter alone should not count.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's challenge to ריש לקיש: redemption is what permits
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks the same kind of question on ריש לקיש: for a blemished קדשים animal, the פדיה permits it, not the שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to ריש לקיש, does the slaughter make it permitted? Doesn't the redemption make it permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר continues and asks the same type of question on ריש לקיש's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished consecrated animal is still holy. Its meat becomes permitted only once it is redeemed with money. So in ריש לקיש's case too, the slaughter is not what makes it permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Redemption of a consecrated animal with money, removing its holiness
But isn't it so that

steps.whatToRemember: Both questions have the same shape: the slaughter is not the final act that permits the meat. For a קרבן it is the זריקה, and for a blemished קדשים animal it is the פדיה.

phrases.english: According to Reish Lakish, does the slaughter permit it?!
But isn't it the redemption that permits it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel challenge to the one on רבי יוחנן, now aimed at ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's case of blemished animals slaughtered outside
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A blemished קדשים animal is permitted only by פדיה, so the slaughter alone should not count.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר forgot רבי שמעון's rule: what is ready is treated as done
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר forgot רבי שמעון's principle: blood ready to be sprinkled counts as sprinkled, and an animal ready to be redeemed counts as redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaching of רבי שמעון escaped him: anything that is ready to be sprinkled is considered as sprinkled, and anything that is ready to be redeemed is considered as redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers both of רבי אלעזר's questions at once with a rule of רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון, once the slaughter leaves the blood ready for זריקה, it is treated as if the blood were already sprinkled. Once a blemished animal is ready for פדיה, it is treated as already redeemed. So the slaughter does count as making the animal permitted, in both רבי יוחנן's and ריש לקיש's cases.

keyTerms.meaning: It escaped him (he forgot it)
Anything that is ready / set to be
Is considered as if sprinkled
Is considered as if redeemed

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's rule (כל העומד לזרוק כזרוק דמי, כל העומד לפדות כפדוי דמי) treats something that is ready to happen as if it already happened. That answers both questions, so both ריש לקיש's and רבי יוחנן's explanations stand.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the meat may actually be eaten before זריקה or פדיה. It only says that, by רבי שמעון's rule, the animal is treated as already sprinkled or redeemed. That is why the slaughter counts.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle of כל העומד treating a coming act as already done shows up across ש״ס and is closely tied to רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: This teaching of Rabbi Shimon escaped him:
Anything that is ready to be sprinkled is considered as sprinkled,
and anything that is ready to be redeemed is considered as redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both of רבי אלעזר's challenges together.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying a known principle that rejects the questioner's assumption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the actual זריקה or פדיה permits the animal, so the slaughter cannot count.
steps.terutzMaskana: By רבי שמעון's rule, what is ready to be sprinkled or redeemed is treated as already done, so the slaughter counts as permitting the animal.

steps.title: Source for the rule: a ברייתא of רבי שמעון about leftover meat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי שמעון holds blood ready to be sprinkled counts as sprinkled. רבי שמעון says some נותר gets טומאת אוכלין and some does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anything that is ready to be sprinkled is treated as if it was already sprinkled. We learn this from a ברייתא: רבי שמעון says there is נותר that can become impure as food, and there is נותר that cannot become impure as food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the principle it just used, כל העומד לזרוק כזרוק דמי. It begins quoting a ברייתא of רבי שמעון that will prove he holds it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only sets up the proof. רבי שמעון splits נותר into two groups: some can get food impurity and some cannot. The next lines explain which is which, and that is where the proof comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Whatever is ready to be sprinkled is treated as already sprinkled
Sacrificial meat left past the time it may be eaten
The kind of impurity that food can get
As it is taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Any blood that is ready to be sprinkled is considered as if sprinkled –
phrases.notes: This is the rule from step 4 that רבי אלעזר forgot. Now the גמרא shows where it comes from.

phrases.english: as it is taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ נוֹתָר שֶׁהוּא מְטַמֵּא טוּמְאַת אוֹכָלִין,
phrases.english: There is leftover meat that can become impure with food impurity,

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ נוֹתָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא טוּמְאַת אוֹכָלִין.
phrases.english: and there is leftover meat that cannot become impure with food impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הָעוֹמֵד לִזְרוֹק כְּזָרוּק דָּמֵי – דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for the principle the גמרא used in step 4 to answer רבי אלעזר.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds blood ready to be sprinkled counts as sprinkled.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי שמעון dividing נותר into meat that can get טומאת אוכלין and meat that cannot.

steps.title: The ברייתא explains: before the sprinkling or after it
steps.stepSummary: Meat left overnight before the זריקה cannot get טומאת אוכלין. Meat left overnight after the זריקה can.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If the meat stayed overnight before the blood was sprinkled, it cannot become impure as food. If it stayed overnight after the sprinkling, it can become impure as food.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains its two kinds of נותר. The dividing line is whether the meat became leftover before or after the blood was sprinkled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the זריקה the meat was never allowed to be eaten, so when it becomes נותר it never had a time of being permitted food. After the זריקה it was permitted for a while, so it counts as food that can become impure. The proof is not finished yet, because the words 'before' and 'after' still need to be explained.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (introduces the details)
Stayed overnight, which makes meat become נותר
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח

phrases.english: How so?
If it stayed overnight before the sprinkling –
it cannot become impure with food impurity.
If it stayed overnight after the sprinkling – it can become impure with food impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא by explaining its two kinds of נותר.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds blood ready to be sprinkled counts as sprinkled.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's rule that meat left overnight after the זריקה can get טומאת אוכלין.

steps.title: 'Before sprinkling' really means before the blood was fit to be sprinkled
steps.stepSummary: An accepted explanation says 'before זריקה' means before the blood was fit for sprinkling, and 'after זריקה' means after it was fit. This completes the proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we hold: What does 'before the sprinkling' mean? Before the blood became fit to be sprinkled. And 'after the sprinkling' means after the blood became fit to be sprinkled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the words of the ברייתא. 'Before' and 'after' sprinkling refer to when the blood became fit to be sprinkled, not to when it was actually sprinkled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat that was left overnight after the blood became fit, even if the blood was never actually sprinkled, still gets טומאת אוכלין. That means the meat is treated as permitted from the moment the blood was ready. That is exactly the rule כל העומד לזרוק כזרוק דמי.

keyTerms.meaning: And we hold (an accepted conclusion)
Fit to be sprinkled

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, once the blood is fit to be sprinkled, the meat is treated as if the blood was already sprinkled. This is the source for כל העומד לזרוק כזרוק דמי.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא says 'after זריקה', but this does not mean the blood was actually sprinkled. It means the blood was ready to be sprinkled, and that is the whole point of the proof.

phrases.english: And we hold:
What does "before the sprinkling" mean –
before it became fit for sprinkling.
"After the sprinkling" – after it became fit for sprinkling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the words of the ברייתא from step 6, which turns it into a proof for the principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Before' and 'after' sprinkling in רבי שמעון's ברייתא mean before and after the blood became fit for sprinkling.

steps.title: When could meat stay overnight before the blood was even fit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case fits 'stayed overnight before the blood was fit for sprinkling'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meat that stayed overnight before the blood was fit for sprinkling: what case is that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a real case of the first half of the ברייתא. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood is normally fit to be sprinkled right after the animal is slaughtered. So it is hard to picture meat that becomes נותר before its blood was ever fit.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (what case is this)

phrases.english: It stayed overnight before it became fit for sprinkling –
what case is that?

steps.triggerLanguage: קוֹדֶם שֶׁנִּרְאָה לִזְרִיקָה לָן – מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a real case that fits the explanation given in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A real case where meat becomes נותר before its blood was ever fit to be sprinkled.

steps.title: Slaughtered right before sunset
steps.stepSummary: The case is where he slaughtered right before sunset, with no time left in the day to sprinkle. That meat cannot get טומאת אוכלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was not enough time left in the day to sprinkle the blood, because he slaughtered the animal right before sunset. So the meat cannot become impure as food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a case: the animal was slaughtered so close to sunset that there was no time left to sprinkle the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood was never fit to be sprinkled, because there was no time left in the day to do it. So the meat was never treated as permitted, and when it became נותר it cannot get טומאת אוכלין.

keyTerms.meaning: Enough time left in the day
Sunset

phrases.english: Where there was not enough time in the day to sprinkle it,
because he slaughtered it close to sunset –
and so it cannot become impure with food impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 with a real case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The animal was slaughtered right before sunset, so the blood was never fit to be sprinkled. The meat therefore cannot get טומאת אוכלין.

steps.title: The case of meat left overnight after the blood was fit for sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The meat stayed overnight when there was still enough time in the day to sprinkle the blood. That meat can get טומאת אוכלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What counts as 'it stayed overnight after the blood was fit for sprinkling'? It is when there was still time left in the day to sprinkle the blood. Then the meat can become impure with טומאת אוכלין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the second case of the ברייתא, the opposite of the case in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, the animal was slaughtered so late that the blood could not be sprinkled that day, so the meat cannot get טומאת אוכלין. Here there was still time to sprinkle, so the blood was 'fit for sprinkling'. Even though nobody actually sprinkled it, the meat can get טומאת אוכלין.

keyTerms.meaning: Enough time, an available window of time
Stayed overnight (used for sacrificial meat left past its time)
The kind of טומאה that food can get

steps.confusionAlert: The blood was NOT actually sprinkled in this case. It only could have been sprinkled. That is the whole point of the proof.

phrases.english: It stayed overnight after it was fit for sprinkling,
when there was time left in the day to sprinkle it,
it can become impure with the impurity of food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from step 9 by defining the opposite case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: After fit for sprinkling means there was still time in the day to sprinkle. Such meat can get טומאת אוכלין.

steps.title: Blood ready to be sprinkled counts as sprinkled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that for רבי שמעון, blood that is ready to be sprinkled is treated as if it was already sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see that anything ready to be sprinkled is considered as if it was already sprinkled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the result of the proof from steps 5 to 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meat can get טומאת אוכלין only if the blood is treated as sprinkled. Here the blood was never really sprinkled, only ready to be. So רבי שמעון must hold that 'ready to be sprinkled' counts as sprinkled. This proves the first half of what the גמרא set out to show.

keyTerms.meaning: Evidently, so we see (introduces a conclusion)
Anything that is ready to be sprinkled
It is considered as if sprinkled

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון: כל העומד לזרוק כזרוק דמי. Blood that could be sprinkled today is treated as if it was already sprinkled.

phrases.english: Evidently, anything that is ready to be sprinkled
is considered as if it was sprinkled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא כָּל הָעוֹמֵד לִזְרוֹק כְּזָרוּק דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the case defined in steps 9 and 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי שמעון holds that blood ready to be sprinkled is treated as if already sprinkled.

steps.title: Second claim: an animal ready to be redeemed counts as redeemed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now shows that רבי שמעון also holds that something ready to be redeemed counts as already redeemed. It opens a ברייתא of רבי שמעון to prove this.
steps.simpleTranslation: And anything ready to be redeemed is considered as if it was already redeemed, as it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second half of its claim and is setting up a new proof. The words of the ברייתא come right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first principle (sprinkling) is now proven. The second principle is about פדיון: an animal that is about to be redeemed is treated as if it was already redeemed. The גמרא only names its source here (דתניא, רבי שמעון אומר), and the actual proof follows next.

keyTerms.meaning: Redeeming something holy so it becomes regular (חולין)
It is considered as if redeemed
As it is taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: And anything that is ready to be redeemed
is considered as if it was redeemed.
As it is taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון's actual words come on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל הָעוֹמֵד לִפְדּוֹת כְּפָדוּי דָּמֵי דְּתַנְיָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving the sprinkling principle, the גמרא turns to the parallel redemption principle.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds כל העומד לפדות כפדוי דמי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי שמעון, whose words come next.
